intro: Step inside Chora, or Kariye, a monastery and church in İstanbul province whose story runs through the 11th–14th century AD. This is the masterpiece of late Byzantine mosaic and fresco, holding the most complete surviving programme of Palaiologan painting. Let your eyes adjust, and look up.
history: The church of the Chora monastery was founded in the eleventh century. Its glory came later: the mosaics and frescoes date from 1315–1321, paid for by the statesman and scholar Theodore Metochites. Scene by scene, they tell the lives of the Virgin and of Christ. And in the side chapel waits the Anastasis, the best-known image in Byzantine painting.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Anastasis fresco and the mosaics of the life of the Virgin. Find your way into the Parekklesion, and look for the Portrait of Metochites.
facts: Did you know? In the mosaic above the door, the donor Theodore Metochites is shown presenting Christ with a model of the building he paid for. A donor holding his own work is rare in Byzantine art. In the side chapel, the Anastasis is the best-known image in Byzantine art: Christ hauls Adam and Eve out of their tombs by the wrists. As for Metochites, his own story took a sad turn. He later lost his fortune and ended his life as a monk in this same monastery, beneath the images he had paid for.
outro: This brings our tour of Chora (Kariye) to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These walls have kept their colours for centuries; let them keep them for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
